title: The 5th lord is exalted, in moolatrikona or in its own sign

text.en: The lord of the 5th house, the bhava of purva punya (merit carried from before this birth), is dignified. Classical texts read a strong 5th lord as merit that is intact and available.
text.impact: In everyday terms, some things come to you more easily than your effort alone explains: help at the right moment, a knack you did not have to learn, goodwill you did not have to earn. The tradition reads that as credit already banked.

text.impact: Whatever you carry forward has somewhere to go in this life. Support tends to arrive through people and openings rather than having to be forced.

title: The 5th lord is in the 6th, 8th or 12th house

text.en: The lord of the 5th house sits in a dusthana, which classical texts read as merit that has to be renewed by effort in this life rather than drawn on freely.
text.impact: Less tends to come for free than for others, and early support can be thin. The tradition's answer is plain: merit is renewable, and service, study and generosity in this life build it back. Effort here is not wasted.

text.impact: Support may feel scarce at the start of life, and recognition slow. This describes the opening position, not the closing one: patience and steady work change it.

text.impact: What looked like a thin start is cancelled. Support tends to appear later, often after a stretch where you had to manage without it.

text.impact: Beliefs handed down to you may not survive contact with your own life, and luck can feel absent in the early stretches. People with this placement often arrive at a steadier conviction of their own later, and value it more for having earned it.

text.impact: A pull towards quiet, solitude and the inner life, and less appetite for display than most people have. The tradition treats this as a settled placement rather than a lack.

text.impact: Letting go tends to take longer for you than for others, whether of places, people or old grievances, and unbroken sleep matters more than you think. Deliberately finishing things, rather than leaving them open, is what helps.

title: The lagna lord is strong in the shashtiamsa (D-60)

text.en: The lord of the lagna is dignified in the shashtiamsa (D-60), the divisional chart Parashara weighs most heavily for karma carried from before this birth.
text.impact: The finest of the divisional charts agrees with the main one here, which the tradition treats as the deepest kind of support. It is sensitive to the exact minute of birth, so it counts only where the birth time is known accurately.
